# decane-connect-kit

> Wallet-connect and non-custodial social sign-in for EVM, Solana, Tron, and Bitcoin dApps, in one npm package (`decane-connect-kit`, MIT license, React 18+ peer dependency, full TypeScript declarations included). Two independent integration paths — wallet-connect (open source, free, no backend) and social sign-in (hosted, requires an API key) — that can be used alone or together through the same `<DecaneKit>` provider and hook API. This file is a self-contained integration spec: everything below is grounded in the actual package source, not paraphrased documentation.

```
npm install decane-connect-kit
```

**Building a React Native / Expo app?** That is a different package with a
different API — no components, no hooks — and its own spec:
https://kit.decane.app/llms-expo.txt (`decane-connect-kit-expo`).

**Verifying users on your own backend?** That is the server-side package
`decane-node`, summarised in Part 3 below — its full self-contained spec is at
https://kit.decane.app/llms-node.txt.

**Shipping apps to your own clients?** If you are an agency, builder or
platform and each client needs their OWN isolated sign-in, there is a
server-to-server provisioning API that creates a project and API key per client
in one call: https://kit.decane.app/llms-connect.txt (`/connect/v1`). You do not
need it for a single product.

---

## Version and freshness

```yaml
version: 2.29.1
document-revision: 2026-09-27
canonical: https://kit.decane.app/llms.txt
version-manifest: https://kit.decane.app/llms-version.json
```

Since 2.4.0 every social account also gets a **Tron** wallet — three wallets
(EVM, Solana, Tron) from one sign-in, all derived from one key. Since 2.5.0 the
SDK records a per-user **transaction history** you can read back. Since 2.6.0
**KingsChat** is a sign-in option alongside email and Google, and login-alone
recovery is always on — a user who reinstalls gets their wallet back from
signing in, so the old `serverAssistedRecovery` option is gone. Server-side
token verification has its own package, **`decane-node`** (see Part 3).
Since 2.26 sessions last **eight hours** and renew themselves while the user is
active (see "Sessions"). Since 2.27 an app can choose the **identity tier**
(`protection: 'identity'`): no passkey, no password, no recovery file — signing
in is the whole ceremony (see "Protection tiers"). Wallet creation now waits
for the enclave to enrol the wallet and throws `WalletEnrolmentError` instead
of leaving a wallet that only ever worked on one device.

`version` is the npm package version whose API surface this document describes.

If you are working from a cached or previously-read copy of this file, compare
its `version` against the one at `version-manifest` — a ~200-byte JSON document
that is cheap to fetch. If the manifest reports a higher version, re-read this
file before relying on it: the API surface has changed. The manifest also lists
what changed in each release, so you can decide whether the delta affects you.

This file is served as a plain-text document at the canonical URL above. It is
not a download — fetch it directly, any time, no auth or headers required.

---

## Part 1 — Wallet connect (open source, free, no backend required)

Detects installed wallets and manages CAIP-25 sessions across chains. Never uses `window.ethereum` — detection is via EIP-6963 (`window.addEventListener('eip6963:announceProvider', ...)`) for EVM, the Solana Wallet Standard for Solana, TronLink's injected provider for Tron, and Unisat/Xverse/OKX-style providers for Bitcoin.

### Minimal working setup

```tsx
import { DecaneKit, useDecane, useWalletSelector, WalletSelector } from 'decane-connect-kit';

// 1. Wrap your app once
function App() {
  return (
    <DecaneKit config={{ mode: 'wallets', theme: 'auto' }}>
      <ConnectButton />
    </DecaneKit>
  );
}

// 2. Open the picker and read connection state from hooks
// <DecaneKit> already renders <WalletSelector> and <SocialWalletModal>
// internally — you never render them yourself, just control them via hooks.
function ConnectButton() {
  const { isConnected, connectedWallet, activeChain, disconnect } = useDecane();
  const { open } = useWalletSelector();

  if (isConnected) {
    return (
      <div>
        Connected: {connectedWallet?.name} on {activeChain}
        <button onClick={disconnect}>Disconnect</button>
      </div>
    );
  }
  return <button onClick={open}>Connect wallet</button>;
}
```

`<DecaneKit config={...}>` takes one `config` prop of type `DecaneConfig`:

```ts
interface DecaneConfig {
  chains?: ChainDescriptor[];               // custom chains to register at init
  supportedChainIds?: string[];             // restrict which built-in chains are available
  networks?: 'evm' | 'solana' | 'tron' | 'bitcoin' | 'all';  // overridden by `mode` when both set
  defaultChain?: string;                    // CAIP-2 id, e.g. 'eip155:1'
  theme?: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto';
  mode?: ConnectMode;                       // see ConnectMode below — default 'wallets'
  social?: SocialConfig;                    // required when mode includes '+social' or is 'social'
}

type ConnectMode =
  | 'all' | 'wallets'          // 'wallets' is the default — all wallet types, no social
  | 'social'                   // social sign-in only, no wallet connect
  | 'evm' | 'solana' | 'tron'  // single chain type, no social
  | 'evm+social' | 'solana+social' | 'tron+social'
  | 'evm+tron' | 'evm+tron+social';
```

### Hooks (all exported from `decane-connect-kit`)

- **`useDecane()`** — connection state: `{ provider, wallets, evmWallets, solanaWallets, multiChainWallets, chains, connectedWallet, activeSession, activeChain, isConnected, theme, setTheme, connect(wallet, preferredChain?), disconnect(), addChain(chain), removeChain(chainId) }`.
- **`useWalletSelector()`** — `{ isOpen, open(), close() }`, controls the built-in `<WalletSelector>` modal.
- **`useChainSwitch()`** — `{ switchChain(chainId): Promise<void>, loading, error, activeChain, grantedChains }`. Extends the current CAIP-25 session to include a new chain (calls `wallet_requestPermissions` under the hood, preserving any existing granted scope for that chain).
- **`useSignMessage()`** — `{ signMessage(message: string, options?: { chainId?, account? }): Promise<string>, signature, loading, error, reset() }`.
- **`useSendTransaction()`** — `{ sendTransaction(tx: TxParams, options?: { chainId?, from? }): Promise<string>, txHash, loading, error, reset() }`, where `TxParams = { to: string; value?: string; data?: string; gas?: string; gasPrice?: string }` (value as decimal or `0x`-hex wei).
- **`useSignTypedData()`** — `{ signTypedData(typedData: { domain, types, message }, options?): Promise<string>, signature, loading, error, reset() }`. EVM only — throws `DecaneErrorCode.EVM_ONLY_METHOD` (5031) if the active chain is Solana/Tron/Bitcoin.

All four signing/session hooks resolve `chainId`/`account` from the active CAIP-25 session when not explicitly passed, and throw a `DecaneError` (see below) on failure — errors are also captured in the hook's own `error` state.

### CAIP-25 session model

Connecting a wallet doesn't itself grant permissions — call `provider.request({ method: 'wallet_requestPermissions', params: [{ requiredScopes: {...}, optionalScopes: {...} }] })` (or use `useChainSwitch().switchChain(chainId)` for the common case of extending to one more chain). A granted scope looks like:

```ts
interface ChainScope {
  methods: CAIP25Method[];  // subset of: wallet_sendTransaction, wallet_signMessage, wallet_signTypedData, wallet_requestPermissions, wallet_revokePermissions, wallet_getPermissions
  accounts: string[];       // CAIP-10, e.g. 'eip155:1:0xAbc...' or 'solana:mainnet:BxY3...'
  events?: string[];
}
```

`provider.activeSession` (`ActiveSession`) exposes `{ sessionId, grantedScopes, walletId, walletType, createdAt }`. Signing on a chain outside the granted scope throws `CHAIN_NOT_IN_SCOPE` (5011).

### Chains

64 built-in chains ship with the package: 59 EVM chains (`eip155:*` — Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum One + Nova, Optimism, BNB Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, plus ~50 more L2s/appchains including Blast, Scroll, zkSync Era, Linea, Mantle, Sei, Monad, Berachain, World Chain, Zora, and others — full list is `BUILT_IN_CHAINS` in the package source), 2 Solana clusters (`solana:mainnet`, `solana:devnet`), 2 Tron networks (`tron:mainnet`, `tron:shasta`), and 1 Bitcoin (`bip122:mainnet`). Named constants for all of them are exported as `CHAINS` (e.g. `CHAINS.ETHEREUM === 'eip155:1'`, `CHAINS.BASE === 'eip155:8453'`).

Register a custom chain (e.g. a local devnet) via `provider.addChain(chain)` or the `config.chains` array:

```ts
provider.addChain({
  id: 'eip155:31337',
  type: 'evm',
  name: 'Localhost',
  chainId: 31337,
  nativeCurrency: { name: 'Ether', symbol: 'ETH', decimals: 18 },
  rpcUrl: 'http://localhost:8545',
  isCustom: true,
});
```

`ChainDescriptor` shape: `{ id: string /* CAIP-2 */; type: 'evm'|'solana'|'tron'|'bitcoin'; name: string; nativeCurrency: { name, symbol, decimals }; rpcUrl?; blockExplorerUrl?; iconUrl?; chainId?: number /* EVM only */; isCustom?: boolean }`.

### `<WalletSelector>` (rendered automatically by `<DecaneKit>`)

Props (for reference — you control it via `useWalletSelector()`, you don't render it yourself): `{ provider, open, onClose, onConnect, theme?, networks?, mode?, socialAuthMethods?, onGoogleSignIn?, onEmailStart?, onEmailVerify? }`.

### Errors

`DecaneError extends Error` with a `code: DecaneErrorCode` field:

| Code | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `USER_REJECTED` | 4001 | User rejected the wallet prompt |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 4100 | Not authorized for the requested method/chain |
| `NO_ACTIVE_SESSION` | 5001 | Signing attempted before any session was granted |
| `SCOPE_MISMATCH` | 5002 | Account not in the granted scope |
| `SESSION_EXPIRED` | 5003 | Session expired, re-request permissions |
| `UNSUPPORTED_CHAIN` | 5010 | Chain not registered (built-in or custom) |
| `CHAIN_NOT_IN_SCOPE` | 5011 | Chain not included in the current granted session |
| `INVALID_CHAIN_CONFIG` | 5012 | Malformed `ChainDescriptor` passed to `addChain` |
| `NO_WALLET_CONNECTED` | 5020 | No wallet connected yet |
| `WALLET_DISCONNECTED` | 5021 | Wallet disconnected mid-operation |
| `PROVIDER_ERROR` | 5022 | Underlying wallet provider threw (wrapped) |
| `METHOD_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 5030 | Unknown/unsupported CAIP-25 method |
| `EVM_ONLY_METHOD` | 5031 | `wallet_signTypedData` called on a non-EVM chain |

---

## Part 2 — Social sign-in (hosted, Google/email embedded wallets)

Non-custodial embedded wallets for users with no wallet installed at all. On first sign-in, a private key is generated client-side and immediately split with Shamir secret sharing into three shares — device (stored in IndexedDB, wrapped by a passkey or PIN), server (encrypted at rest on the key server), and recovery (the user's to keep) — any two of which reconstruct the key; one alone reveals nothing. Signing happens inside a TEE (Trusted Execution Environment, a hardware-isolated enclave) which reconstructs the key only in isolated memory, verifies it controls the account's recorded wallet, signs, and discards it — the full private key never exists in plaintext outside that enclave, and never touches the server's own process memory or disk. Requires an API key from the developer dashboard (has its own pricing — Free/Scale/Enterprise tiers, see https://kit.decane.app/pricing).

### Standalone usage (no React)

```ts
import { createDecaneConnect } from 'decane-connect-kit';

const connect = await createDecaneConnect({
  apiKey: 'dck_live_...',
  chains: ['evm:1', 'solana:mainnet'],       // Chain = `evm:${number}` | `solana:'mainnet'|'devnet'`
  authMethods: ['google', 'email'],
});

const { addresses, isNewUser, profile } = await connect.connectWithGoogle();
// addresses: { evm?: string; solana?: string }
// profile:   { name?: string; email?: string; picture?: string } | undefined

const sig = await connect.signMessage({ chain: 'evm:1', message: 'hello' });
const txHash = await connect.sendTransaction({ chain: 'evm:1', to: '0x...', value: 1000000000000000n });

// ERC-20 transfer = a contract call: `to` is the token contract, value 0n, `data` is the encoded transfer().
import { Interface, parseUnits } from 'ethers';
const data = new Interface(['function transfer(address,uint256)'])
  .encodeFunctionData('transfer', [recipient, parseUnits('1.5', 6)]); // 6 = token decimals
const erc20Hash = await connect.sendTransaction({ chain: 'evm:1', to: TOKEN_ADDRESS, value: 0n, data });

// Solana: sendTransaction is EVM-only. Build + serialize an unsigned tx, sign it (returns
// broadcast-ready bytes), then broadcast yourself via @solana/web3.js:
const signed = await connect.signSolanaTransaction(serializedUnsignedTx); // Uint8Array -> signed Uint8Array
// await new Connection(rpcUrl).sendRawTransaction(signed);
```

`createDecaneConnect(config: DecaneConnectConfig): Promise<DecaneConnect>` throws a plain `Error` (not `DecaneConnectError`) if `apiKey` is missing or `chains` is empty.

**`DecaneConnectConfig`** (full shape):

```ts
interface DecaneConnectConfig {
  apiKey: string;
  chains: Chain[];
  authMethods: Array<'google' | 'email'>;
  apiBaseUrl?: string;                // default: https://api.decane.app — self-host override only
  sessionDurationMinutes?: number;    // default: 120 (capped by the JWT and signer TTL)
  promptPin?: () => Promise<string>;  // required if the browser has no passkey support
  rpId?: string;                      // WebAuthn RP ID, defaults to window.location.hostname
  rpName?: string;                    // WebAuthn RP display name
  rpcUrls?: Record<string, string>;   // override built-in public RPCs per chain
  teeUrl?: string;                    // advanced/self-hosted override only
  // Require a fresh passkey assertion for EVERY signature (TEE-verified,
  // single-use 60s challenge) instead of letting an unlocked session sign
  // freely until expiry. Does NOT shorten the session — see "Signing
  // authority model" below. Default false. Needs a passkey; PIN-only wallets
  // have no authenticator to assert with and signing fails rather than
  // falling back. Also available as SocialConfig.requireAssertionPerSignature
  // on the React <DecaneKit> path.
  requireAssertionPerSignature?: boolean;
  // How this device holds its share of the wallet — see "Protection tiers".
  // 'device' (default): wrapped at rest under a passkey or the unlock password.
  // 'identity': nothing stored, nothing asked; every visit is a sign-in and the
  // enclave provisions a fresh share against it. Same key either way.
  protection?: 'identity' | 'device';
  /** @deprecated alias for protection: 'identity' */
  deferDeviceProtection?: boolean;
  // Resume the live session in a NEW tab, not only after a reload. Default
  // false in the device tier, true in the identity tier. The session handle is
  // the signing credential, so this widens where it can be read from one tab
  // to the whole origin — pair with requireAssertionPerSignature if that matters.
  resumeSessionAcrossTabs?: boolean;
  persistSession?: boolean;           // default true — reload resumes the session
  // Recovery. The key is split 2-of-3 (device/server/recovery). A user on a new
  // device is restored by signing in (the enclave holds a sealed share — "Flow
  // S"); a synced passkey (Flow A) and a saved recovery file (Flow B) are the
  // fallbacks. Flow B requires the two callbacks marked below.
  offerRecoveryAtSignup?: boolean;    // default false since 2.7.4 — opt in to offer a recovery file at signup
  onRecoveryShareOffer?: (addresses: { evmAddress: string; solanaAddress: string })
    => Promise<{ wants: boolean; password?: string; passwordHint?: string }>;
  onRecoveryFileReady?: (file: RecoveryShareFile, filename: string) => Promise<void>;
  promptForRecoveryFile?: () => Promise<{ file: RecoveryShareFile; password: string } | null>; // Flow B
  onRecoveryRotated?: (addresses: { evmAddress: string; solanaAddress: string })
    => Promise<{ password: string; passwordHint?: string }>;  // Flow B — REQUIRED; recovery throws without it
  onRecoveryProgress?: (event: RecoveryProgress) => void;
}
```

**`DecaneConnect`** (the object `createDecaneConnect` resolves to) — full method set:

```ts
interface DecaneConnect {
  connect(): Promise<ConnectResult>;                              // opens whichever authMethods are configured
  connectWithGoogle(): Promise<ConnectResult>;
  connectWithEmail(email: string): Promise<{ codeRequired: true }>;
  verifyEmailCode(email: string, code: string): Promise<ConnectResult>;
  connectWithToken(token: string, opts?: { providerId?: string }): Promise<ConnectResult>; // custom auth — see below
  unlock(): Promise<void>;                                        // re-authenticate an expired session
  isUnlocked(): boolean;
  sessionExpiresAt(): number | null;
  signMessage(req: SignMessageRequest): Promise<string>;        // EVM, Solana, or Tron chain. message: string | Uint8Array — on EVM/Tron the enclave hashes TEXT, so bytes must be valid UTF-8 (decoded losslessly; SIWE and every hex personal_sign a dApp sends qualify) or the call throws CallSequenceError. Solana signs raw bytes.
  sendTransaction(req: SendTransactionRequest): Promise<string>; // EVM; auto-records to history
  signSolanaTransaction(tx: Uint8Array): Promise<Uint8Array>;
  signTronTransaction(rawDataHex: string): Promise<string>;      // sign a TronWeb-built tx's raw_data
  recordTransaction(tx: RecordTransactionInput): Promise<TransactionRecord>;  // record a tx you broadcast
  getTransactionHistory(limit?: number): Promise<TransactionRecord[]>;        // most recent first
  disconnect(): Promise<void>;
  getAddresses(): { evm?: string; solana?: string; tron?: string } | null;   // three wallets
  rotateShares(opts: { password: string; passwordHint?: string }): Promise<RecoveryShareFile>;      // new recovery file; invalidates the old one. Needs a fresh WebAuthn assertion.
  exportPortableBackup(opts: { password: string; passwordHint?: string }): Promise<PortableBackup>; // two-share bearer file (device+recovery); also rotates the set
  hasRecoveryShare(): Promise<boolean>;                            // UX flag — has the user ever saved a recovery file
  shouldPromptRecovery(): Promise<boolean>;                        // true at most once — time to nudge saving one
  dismissRecoveryPrompt(): Promise<void>;                          // call regardless of answer; the nudge fires once ever
  hasBackup(): Promise<boolean>;                                   // is a server-side wrapped-share backup present (Flow A)
  deleteBackup(): Promise<void>;                                   // delete it — disables Flow A passkey-sync recovery
  on(event: SdkEvent, handler: (...args: unknown[]) => void): void;
  off(event: SdkEvent, handler: (...args: unknown[]) => void): void;
}
// ConnectResult = { addresses: { evm?: string; solana?: string; tron?: string }; isNewUser: boolean; profile?: AuthProfile }
// AuthProfile   = { name?: string; email?: string; picture?: string }  — pass-through from the provider, never stored
// SdkEvent = 'connected' | 'disconnected' | 'session-expired' | 'session-renewed' | 'session-started'
//          | 'wallet-creating' | 'wallet-unlocking' | 'enrolment-failed' | 'migrated-to-identity'
// TransactionRecord = { id, chain, kind, txHash, to, value, status, metadata, createdAt }
// RecordTransactionInput = { chain, txHash?, to?, value?, kind?, status?, metadata? }
```

**Three wallets from one sign-in.** Every account has an EVM address, a Solana
address, and a Tron address — the Tron and EVM addresses share one secp256k1 key
(Tron is the EVM address re-encoded), so there is no extra key to manage.
`getAddresses()` returns all three. Tron uses CAIP-style chain ids
`tron:mainnet` (also `tron:shasta` / `tron:nile`); `signMessage` accepts a Tron
chain, and `signTronTransaction(rawDataHex)` signs a transaction you built with
TronWeb (the enclave computes the txID and signs — you broadcast the result).

**Transaction history.** `sendTransaction` records itself automatically. For
Solana/Tron transactions your dApp broadcasts, call
`recordTransaction({ chain, txHash, to?, value?, metadata? })` so they appear in
the user's history; read it back with `getTransactionHistory()`. This is a plain
data API — the SDK renders no history UI; you build it. Records are keyed by
`(user, txHash)`, so re-recording a hash with a new `status` updates in place.

Email sign-in is the two-step `connectWithEmail(email)` → `verifyEmailCode(email, code)` flow — a 6-digit code is emailed, `connectWithEmail` always resolves the same way regardless of whether the address has an account (prevents email enumeration).

> Note: the package also exports standalone `startEmailAuth`/`verifyEmailCode` functions, but their first parameter is an internal `ApiClient` type that isn't part of the public API — use `DecaneConnect.connectWithEmail()`/`.verifyEmailCode()` instead (shown above), not the standalone functions.

### React usage

```tsx
import { DecaneKit, useSocialAuth, SocialWalletModal } from 'decane-connect-kit';

function App() {
  return (
    <DecaneKit config={{
      mode: 'social',                    // or 'all' / 'evm+social' etc. to combine with wallet-connect
      social: { apiKey: 'dck_live_...', authMethods: ['google', 'email'] },
    }}>
      <SignInButton />
    </DecaneKit>
  );
}

function SignInButton() {
  const { isConnected, addresses, signInWithGoogle, googleLoading } = useSocialAuth();
  if (isConnected) return <div>Signed in: {addresses?.evm}</div>;
  return <button onClick={signInWithGoogle} disabled={googleLoading}>Sign in with Google</button>;
}
```

- **`useSocialAuth()`** — sign-in flow: `{ isConnected, isUnlocked, isNewUser, profile, providerSubject, addresses, sessionExpiresAt, needsReconnect, canUsePasskey, phase: "creating" | "unlocking" | null, isCreatingWallet, googleLoading, kingschatLoading, xLoading, emailLoading, phoneLoading, tokenLoading, customLoading, customAuthLabel, error, clearError(), signInWithGoogle(), signInWithKingsChat(), signInWithX(), sendEmailCode(email): Promise<{codeRequired:true}>, confirmEmailCode(email, code), sendPhoneCode(phone): Promise<{codeRequired:true}>, confirmPhoneCode(phone, code), signInWithToken(token, opts?), signInWithAccessToken(token), signInWithCustomAuth?(), signInWithPasskey(), unlock(), disconnect() }`. `signInWithCustomAuth` is `undefined` unless `social.customAuth` is configured. `canUsePasskey` is true when this device can sign the remembered user back in with one passkey prompt — see "Signing back in after sign-out".
- **`useSocialWallet()`** — sign-in + signing + modal control: everything in `useSocialAuth()` plus `{ modalOpen, openModal(), closeModal(), signMessage(chain, message), sendTransaction(req), signTypedData(req), signAuthorization(req), signSolanaTransaction(tx), signTronTransaction(rawDataHex), getEthereumProvider(opts?): Eip1193Provider, getBalance(chain?), getBalances(), recordTransaction(tx), getTransactionHistory(limit?), getAccessToken(): string | null, hasPasskey(), addPasskey(), deviceProtected(), protectDevice(), setUnlockPassword(password), canUnlockWithPassword(), unlockWithPassword(password), removeUnlockPassword(), forgetLastUser(), rotateShares({ password, passwordHint? }), exportPortableBackup({ password, passwordHint? }), hasRecoveryShare(), shouldPromptRecovery(), dismissRecoveryPrompt(), loading, error, clearError() }`. Passkey and password methods are per DEVICE: `addPasskey`/`setUnlockPassword` need a live session; `canUnlockWithPassword`/`unlockWithPassword` and `signInWithPasskey` are the signed-out pair that open one without an identity provider.

`<SocialWalletModal>` is rendered automatically by `<DecaneKit>` (props: `{ open, onClose, theme?, socialAuth, onUnlock, onDisconnect }`) — control it via `useSocialWallet().openModal()`/`.closeModal()`, don't render it directly.

### Signing back in after sign-out

`disconnect()` ends the session (revokes the JWT, drops it) but deliberately keeps the device's passkey-wrapped or password-wrapped share, so a returning user is one prompt from a session instead of a full sign-in. Since 2.22 it also remembers WHICH account signed out. That is what lets `canUsePasskey` / `canUnlockWithPassword` offer that account's own way back even when several accounts are enrolled on the same browser — before, with more than one enrolled, the kit refused to guess and both read false. The remembered id is a lookup key, not a credential: `signInWithPasskey` still needs a server-verified WebAuthn assertion and `unlockWithPassword` still needs the password.

- Offer the shortcut when `canUsePasskey` (prefer it) or `await canUnlockWithPassword()` is true; fall back to the full method list otherwise.
- "Use a different account" = `forgetLastUser()`. It drops the memory so the previous account stops being offered, and recomputes `canUsePasskey`. Device shares are untouched.
- Only the explicit entry points consult the memory. `connect()`/`unlock()` keep the strict lookup, so an ordinary sign-in never silently re-offers the account the user just left.

### Sessions — since 2.26.0

An access token lasts **eight hours**. The SDK renews it at 75% of its life
while the user is active (`POST /auth/refresh`, emitting `session-renewed`),
and the backend caps the chain at **seven days** from the sign-in, after which
the user signs in again. The enclave's signing session has its own life; when
it lapses with the token still valid, `unlock()` reopens it without a sign-in
(no prompt in the identity tier; the passkey/password in the device tier).
With `resumeSessionAcrossTabs` a new tab resumes the live session instead of
reading as signed out. `disconnect()` stops the renewal.

### Protection tiers — since 2.27.0 (`deferDeviceProtection` since 2.23.0)

Every wallet is a 2-of-3 split {device, server, recovery}. At creation the
recovery share is sealed by the enclave ("enrolment"); with it, `/signer/provision`
hands any signed-in session a fresh device share on the JWT alone. The tier is
**how this device holds that share** — never which key the wallet is.

| | `protection: 'device'` (default) | `protection: 'identity'` |
|---|---|---|
| At creation | share wrapped under a passkey (or `promptUnlockPassword`) | nothing stored, nothing asked |
| Later visits | passkey/password unlock, or sign in | sign in; the enclave provisions |
| `requireAssertionPerSignature` | available | not applicable |
| Lost device | sign in again | sign in again |

**The identity tier's security statement, verbatim:** a wallet is exactly as
safe as the user's identity-provider account plus Decane (the JWT signing key
and the attested enclave). Anyone who can obtain a valid Decane session for the
user can sign. There is no device-bound factor. Mitigations: a new-device email
on every provision from an unseen device, a per-user freeze switch operated by
Decane, and (follow-up) a fresh sign-in requirement for high-value operations.
Do not choose it where a stolen Google session must not be enough to move funds.

- The tier belongs to **this client, not the wallet**: two apps on one project
  can hold the same wallet in different tiers (a marketplace with passkeys, a
  social app without). Same key, same addresses. A per-signature assertion
  declared by one app protects that app's sessions, not the wallet.
- Switching an app to `'identity'` ports users on their next sign-in with no
  loss of funds: an enrolled wallet provisions silently; one never enrolled but
  holding a wrapped share on this device is unlocked ONE last time, enrolled,
  and never prompted again (`migrated-to-identity` fires). Nothing is re-split,
  rotated or moved.
- In the identity tier `canSignInWithPasskey()` is false, `signInWithPasskey()`
  and `addPasskey()` throw `CallSequenceError`, `protectDevice()` is a no-op
  returning false, and `offerRecoveryAtSignup` is ignored.
- The device tier keeps the deferred pattern for apps that want the passkey
  asked at their own moment: `deviceProtected()` / `protectDevice()` on
  `useSocialWallet()` — `protectDevice()` needs a live session, provisions a
  share from the enclave if the device has none, wraps it (passkey, else
  password), resolves false on a dismissed prompt, and is idempotent.
- **Creation waits for enrolment, in every tier** (since 2.27.0): the server
  share is uploaded as provisional, the enclave seals the recovery share (three
  attempts, no retry on 429/403), and only then does the session open. On
  failure the SDK throws `WalletEnrolmentError`, deletes any share it stored,
  and the backend still reports no wallet — the next sign-in creates afresh.
  Before, a failed enrolment left a wallet that could never be provisioned to
  another device. The server's `wallet_created` event records the tier as
  `unlockMethod: "identity" | "passkey" | "password"`.

### Handing a session to another app of the same project — since 2.24.0

Two apps of one Decane project are one identity, and often one host (`/` and `/square`). Since 2.24.0 the client keys everything it persists — the remembered identity, the last signed-out user, the live session — by the **app id**, not the API key, so two apps under different keys on one origin see the same signed-in user, and a same-tab navigation between them resumes the full session with no prompt. (What an older build wrote under the key is read once and moved.)

For everything else — a new tab, a different origin, a lapsed session — the sending app puts its access token in the URL and the receiving app adopts it:

```ts
// sender: the same token every API call carries as a Bearer
location.assign(`/square?decane_token=${encodeURIComponent(getAccessToken()!)}`);

// receiver, on load
const token = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("decane_token");
if (token) {
  history.replaceState(null, "", location.pathname);   // out of the address bar at once
  if (!isConnected) await signInWithAccessToken(token); // useSocialAuth()
}
```

- `connectWithAccessToken(token)` / `signInWithAccessToken(token)`: signed in at once — `addresses`, `getAccessToken()` and every Bearer call work — but **not unlocked**. The first `unlock()` or signing call provisions or unwraps the device share as an ordinary returning sign-in would; with `deferDeviceProtection` that prompts for nothing.
- The backend judges the token: a revoked or foreign one throws `InvalidAccessTokenError` (`INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN`), as does one that is expired or not a Decane token. The session lasts as long as the token (at most two hours); when it lapses the client emits `session-expired` and `needsReconnect` reads true.
- Strip the parameter from the URL immediately and never log it: it is a bearer credential for its remaining lifetime.

### Signing authority model — per-signature assertion since 2.2.0

Two modes, and the distinction matters when comparing against other embedded-wallet SDKs.

**Default (session authority).** `unlock()` opens a TEE session with a TTL (`sessionDurationMinutes`, default 120; the effective lifetime is the shortest of this, the JWT expiry and the signer TTL, so `sessionExpiresAt` is the value to trust). For that window a live session is sufficient authority: signatures need no further prompt. Authority is bounded by *time* and dies on expiry or `pagehide` — it is not standing.

**`requireAssertionPerSignature: true` (per-signature authority).** The session still stays warm — this is the point, since tearing it down would cost a fresh TDX attestation and a full re-auth per signature — but a live session stops being sufficient. Each signature requires a fresh WebAuthn assertion answered against a single-use, 60-second challenge, verified *inside the enclave* (the same gate already protecting `rotateShares` / `exportPortableBackup`). Client-side refusal is not the mechanism; the TEE will not sign without it.

```ts
// standalone
await createDecaneConnect({ apiKey, chains, authMethods, requireAssertionPerSignature: true });
// React
<DecaneKit config={{ social: { apiKey, requireAssertionPerSignature: true } }}>
```

Consequences worth stating explicitly:

- **It does not shorten the session.** The countdown is unchanged; `sessionDurationMinutes` is the separate knob for that. Turning this on and expecting a shorter timer is the common misreading.
- **Multi-step flows prompt per leg.** ERC-20 approve + swap is two prompts.
- **Requires a passkey.** PIN-only wallets fail rather than degrade.
- **A declined prompt is not an expired session.** It surfaces as `ExportNotAuthorizedError` and the session handle stays valid, so no reconnect is forced.
- **Scope limit, stated plainly:** the policy is declared by the client at session open. It makes a leaked session *handle* worthless without the authenticator, but a fully compromised page could open a session without the flag. Server-sourced policy (per user / per project) would be needed to make it unbypassable; not implemented.

Requires TEE signer v0.2.3+. Sessions that don't opt in behave exactly as before, so older clients are unaffected.

### Custom auth (bring your own JWT issuer) — since 2.1.0

Instead of Google/email, a dApp can sign users in with a token from its own identity system (Auth0, Clerk, Firebase, Cognito, or its own backend). The developer registers an issuer + JWKS URL against their project in the dashboard; the SDK exchanges a token that issuer already signed for a Decane session. Everything downstream — wallet creation, signing, recovery — is identical to Google/email sign-in. Decane never sees a credential, only a signed token, its issuer, and one claim.

The user's wallet is derived from `HMAC(providerId + ':' + <identity claim value>)`, so the same claim value always resolves to the same wallet. The dashboard therefore treats `issuer` and `identity_claim` as immutable after creation, and refuses to delete a provider that has users (disable it instead) — changing either would silently re-identify existing users onto empty wallets.

Two ways to use it:

```tsx
// A. Built-in UI — renders a button in WalletSelector and SocialWalletModal
//    alongside Google/email. getToken() runs when the user clicks it.
<DecaneKit config={{
  appId: '<project id>',
  mode: 'all',
  social: {
    apiKey: 'dck_live_...',
    authMethods: ['google', 'email'],
    customAuth: {
      label: 'Continue with Acme Inc',    // button text
      providerId: undefined,              // only needed with >1 provider configured
      getToken: async () => (await myAuthClient.getSession()).accessToken,
    },
  },
}}>{children}</DecaneKit>

// B. Headless — you already have the token, drive your own UI
const { signInWithToken, tokenLoading } = useSocialAuth();
await signInWithToken(token /*, { providerId } */);

// ...or with no React at all:
const { addresses, isNewUser } = await connect.connectWithToken(token);

`profile` carries who the provider says the user is — `{ name?, email?, picture? }`
— and is **absent** when the provider released nothing (email sign-in always, and
Google when the user withheld it). Decane never stores it: the backend keeps only
an HMAC and a masked identifier, so there is no profile to fetch later. Cache what
you need at sign-in if you want to greet the user by name after a reload.
```

`SocialConfig.customAuth?: { label: string; providerId?: string; getToken: () => Promise<string> }`.

`providerId` is only required when a project has more than one enabled provider — with several configured the backend will not guess, because trying each issuer in turn would let a token from a weak provider be accepted as if it came from a strong one.

The backend (`POST /auth/external`) verifies, in order: signature against the published JWKS (key rotation handled automatically — an unrecognized `kid` triggers a refetch), issuer, expiry, audience if one is configured, and that the identity claim is a non-empty string or number. Failures 1–4 collapse into one opaque `INVALID_TOKEN` so error messages can't be used to probe for forgeable gaps. Config-level problems report distinctly: `NO_PROVIDER`, `AMBIGUOUS_PROVIDER`, `MISSING_CLAIM`.

The JWKS URL must return a standard key set and must be `https://` (or localhost in dev) — a downgraded fetch would let an on-path attacker serve a forged key set and mint tokens for any user:

```json
{ "keys": [ { "kty": "RSA", "kid": "key-1", "use": "sig", "alg": "RS256", "n": "0vx7ago...", "e": "AQAB" } ] }
```

EC keys work too (`kty: "EC"`, `crv`, `x`, `y` instead of `n`/`e`). The `kid` must match the JWT header's `kid`. Multiple keys in the array is how rotation works.

### Errors

All extend `DecaneConnectError` (`{ code: string; message: string; retryable: boolean }`):

| Class | code | retryable | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InvalidApiKeyError` | `INVALID_API_KEY` | no | API key is invalid or revoked |
| `OriginNotAllowedError` | `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED` | no | Calling origin isn't in the API key's allowlist |
| `SessionExpiredError` | `SESSION_EXPIRED` | yes | Session TTL elapsed — call `unlock()` |
| `UnlockRequiredError` | `UNLOCK_REQUIRED` | yes | Signing attempted before unlocking |
| `ReconnectRequiredError` | `RECONNECT_REQUIRED` | yes | Session ended and JWT expired — sign in again |
| `UserCancelledError` | `USER_CANCELLED` | yes | User dismissed a passkey/PIN/OAuth prompt |
| `WebAuthnNotSupportedError` | `WEBAUTHN_UNSUPPORTED` | no | Browser has no WebAuthn support and no `promptPin` configured |
| `InvalidPinError` | `INVALID_PIN` | yes | Incorrect PIN entered |
| `CallSequenceError` | `CALL_SEQUENCE` | no | SDK methods called out of order (e.g. signing before connecting) |
| `NetworkError` | `NETWORK` | yes | Request to the backend failed |
| `ShareCorruptedError` | `SHARE_CORRUPTED` | no | Locally stored device share is corrupted |
| `NewDeviceError` | `NEW_DEVICE` | no | No device share found on this device — re-authenticate to provision it |
| `PromptPinNotConfiguredError` | `PROMPT_PIN_NOT_CONFIGURED` | no | Passkey unavailable and no `promptPin` callback was provided |
| `AttestationError` | `ATTESTATION_FAILED` | no | TEE attestation quote failed verification |
| `RecoveryFailedError` | `RECOVERY_FAILED` | yes | Recovery flow failed |
| `InvalidRecoveryFileError` | `INVALID_RECOVERY_FILE` | no | Uploaded file isn't a valid recovery file |
| `WrongPasswordError` | `WRONG_PASSWORD` | yes | Incorrect password for the recovery file |
| `RecoveryWalletMismatchError` | `RECOVERY_WALLET_MISMATCH` | no | Recovery file is for a different wallet than the signed-in account |
| `ExportNotAuthorizedError` | `EXPORT_NOT_AUTHORIZED` | yes | Export needs a fresh security check first |
| `WalletEnrolmentError` | `WALLET_ENROLMENT_FAILED` | yes | Creation stopped: the enclave did not seal the wallet's share. Nothing was created — sign in again (2.27.0) |
| `ProvisioningRateLimitedError` | `PROVISIONING_RATE_LIMITED` | yes | `/signer/provision` answered 429 — too many devices/tabs this hour; the wallet is fine, wait and sign in again. Never a new-device dead end (2.27.0) |
| `EnclaveHttpError` | `ENCLAVE_HTTP` | 5xx only | Any other non-OK enclave answer; `.status` carries the HTTP status (2.27.0) |
| `StaleDeviceShareError` | `STALE_DEVICE_SHARE` | yes | This device's share is from a superseded set; cleared, re-recover |
| `InvalidAccessTokenError` | `INVALID_ACCESS_TOKEN` | no | `connectWithAccessToken` given a revoked or foreign token |

---

## Part 3 — Server-side token verification (`decane-node`)

When a signed-in user calls your own backend, send the Decane access token
(`getAccessToken()` on the client) as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and verify
it server-side with the **`decane-node`** package — the `@privy-io/node`
equivalent. `npm install decane-node` (Node 18+).

```ts
import { DecaneClient } from 'decane-node';

// Two verification modes:
//  1. Static verification key (Privy-style, offline) — copy your project's ES256
//     public key from the dashboard (API Keys page) into DECANE_VERIFICATION_KEY.
//  2. JWKS (default) — omit the key; the SDK fetches/caches Decane's public JWKS.
// appId is checked against the token's project_id (the audience-equivalent).
const decane = new DecaneClient({
  appId: process.env.DECANE_APP_ID,
  verificationKey: process.env.DECANE_VERIFICATION_KEY, // optional; JWKS if unset
});

const claims = await decane.verifyAccessToken(token);   // throws DecaneAuthError if invalid
claims.userId;                                           // stable Decane user id (uid)

// Or fail-closed without throwing, and resolve addresses:
const safe = await decane.safeVerifyAccessToken(token); // DecaneClaims | null
const user = await decane.getUser(token);               // { id, addresses, linkedAccounts }
```

`verificationKey` also reads from the `DECANE_VERIFICATION_KEY` env var, so a
backend can pass only `appId` in code. A standalone
`verifyAccessToken({ token, appId, verificationKey })` is also exported for a
drop-in replacement of Privy's function. npm:
https://www.npmjs.com/package/decane-node

Since decane-node 1.2.0 the server can also **sign users in** — email OTP,
Google/KingsChat token exchange, and custom-auth JWT exchange run as pure HTTP
with the project's `dck_` API key (`new DecaneClient({ appId, apiKey })` then
`connectWithEmail`/`verifyEmailCode`, `connectWithGoogleToken`,
`connectWithKingsChatToken`, `connectWithToken`). Browser-bound flows (Google
redirect, KingsChat popup, passkeys) and wallet creation/signing remain
client-side.

This is a summary. The full `decane-node` spec — sign-in methods, verification
modes, error codes, config env fallbacks, revocation caveats, Privy migration —
is its own self-contained document at https://kit.decane.app/llms-node.txt (human
docs: https://kit.decane.app/node-docs).
